MaxEmotionHistorySamples.blurb: How many past samples of each mood emotion (stimulated, confident, etc.) Vector keeps in a circular history buffer. Default 128. Used so mood code can ask “what was this emotion N ticks or N seconds ago?” when scoring mood deltas and events.
MaxEmotionHistorySamples.detail: Each Emotion object constructs its CircularBuffer with this capacity and re-sizes on Emotion::Reset() (MoodManager reset path). On every Emotion::Update tick a new HistorySample is pushed; older samples fall off when full. GetHistoryValueTicksAgo / GetHistoryValueSecondsAgo and the delta helpers read this buffer (e.g. MoodManager stim/conf comparisons). Changing the console value mid-run does not resize existing buffers until Reset (or a new Emotion is constructed) — so a hot tweak alone will not grow or shrink the live history.
MaxEmotionHistorySamples.statusNote: Capacity is applied only at Emotion construction and Reset(). Live buffer size does not follow console changes until the next Reset.

MaxExpectedTimeBetweenCapturedFrames_ms.blurb: How long (milliseconds) the engine will wait without a new camera frame before logging a warning that capture is stalled. Default 500 ms. Does not change exposure, restart the camera, or drop frames — it only gates a diagnostic log line.
MaxExpectedTimeBetweenCapturedFrames_ms.detail: In VisionComponent::CaptureImage, after a failed CameraGetFrame when capture is supposed to be running (not waiting for a format change, not in power-save, and at least one frame has been captured before), if current basestation time exceeds last capture time by this many ms, it prints VisionComponent.CaptureImage.TooLongSinceFrameWasCaptured with last/now timestamps. Useful when hunting freezes or camera service hang-ups; raising it reduces false positives under load; lowering it logs sooner.
MaxExpectedTimeBetweenCapturedFrames_ms.statusNote: Live for logging only — no recovery or capture-policy change.

MaxFractionOverexposed.blurb: When auto-exposure looks at the brightness histogram, if more than this fraction of sampled pixels are overexposed (default 0.8 = 80%), exposure is cut hard using OverExposedAdjustmentFraction instead of the normal target-percentile adjustment. Range 0–1.
MaxFractionOverexposed.detail: CameraParamsController::ComputeAdjustmentFraction counts the top histogram bin (pixels above OverExposedThreshold, default 240) versus total samples. If fractionOverexposed exceeds this threshold, adjustmentFraction is set to kOverExposedAdjustmentFraction (default 0.5) so the next exposure/gain step drops quickly in blow-out lighting. Below the threshold, normal percentile→target math runs (or cycling AE targets). Part of Vision.PreProcessing console group alongside under/over thresholds and center-weighted metering. Coretech vision library used by engine AE.

MaxNumInitialReactAttemptsBeforeGivingUp.blurb: While Vector is held in a palm and drives both front (or both rear) cliff sensors over the palm edge, how many failed initial edge-react animations/actions are allowed before the robot gives up and runs the “stuck on palm edge / ask for help” path. Default 2.
MaxNumInitialReactAttemptsBeforeGivingUp.detail: BehaviorReactToPalmEdge (category Behavior.ReactToPalmEdge). On each initial reaction attempt, numInitialReactAttempts is incremented. Before starting another attempt, if the counter exceeds this limit, TransitionToStuckOnPalmEdge runs (delegates to askForHelpBehavior). Prevents thrashing forever in a “cliffy” palm orientation or when StuckOnPalmEdge is not otherwise detecting the pose. Only matters when the held-in-palm palm-edge reaction is active.

MaxNumRobotStopsBeforeGivingUp.blurb: During cliff reaction, how many cliff-related RobotStopped events Vector will tolerate before quitting recovery backups/animations and going to StuckOnEdge / ask-for-help. Default 5. Protects against thrashing on a very cliffy surface.
MaxNumRobotStopsBeforeGivingUp.detail: BehaviorReactToCliff (category Behavior.ReactToCliff) listens for EngineToGame RobotStopped with StopReason::CLIFF and increments persistent numStops. When TransitionToPlayingCliffReaction runs, if numStops exceeds this limit it logs TooManyRobotStops and TransitionToStuckOnEdge. Separate from MaxNumCliffReactAttemptsBeforeGivingUp (animation/action failure count, default 2). Only active while ReactToCliff is activated.

MaxRobotAngleChangeDuringBackup_rad.blurb: Factory playpen test: maximum allowed yaw change (radians) while the robot backs up after placing a cube. Default about 10° (DEG_TO_RAD(10)). If the robot twists more than this during backup or the triple-backup anim, the pickup-cube playpen step fails (BACKUP_NOT_STRAIGHT / BACK_AND_FORTH_NOT_STRAIGHT).
MaxRobotAngleChangeDuringBackup_rad.detail: PlaypenConfig static, exposed via WRAP_EXTERN_CONSOLE_VAR under category Playpen. BehaviorPlaypenPickupCube records yaw at pickup, then after PlaceObjectOnGroundAction and after anim_triple_backup compares absolute Z-angle change to this limit. Used only in factory/dev playpen, not freeplay. Units are radians in the console (default ~0.175 rad).

NumTimesToSeeFrontalToBeStable.blurb: How many times an unnamed face must be observed looking toward the camera before FaceWorld treats it as a “stable session-only” face (default 30). Named faces are stable immediately; tracking-only IDs never are.
NumTimesToSeeFrontalToBeStable.detail: FaceEntry::HasStableID requires positive face ID and either a name or numTimesObservedFacingCamera ≥ this threshold. On the observation that crosses the threshold for an unnamed recognized ID, FaceWorld emits a one-shot DAS event (robot.vision.face_recognition.persistent_session_only) and bumps the frontal counter so it does not re-fire. Stable IDs also gate re-see DAS logging (TimeUnobservedBeforeReLoggingToDAS_ms). Lower values mark strangers stable sooner (more DAS/telemetry); higher values demand longer frontal observation.

Obstacles.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::Obstacles. When on, each vision tick runs the ground-plane classifier on the color camera image to mark free vs non-drivable ground, producing visual obstacle edge frames that the nav map can add as detected obstacles.
Obstacles.detail: Auto-registered bool under Vision.General.VisionModes by SetupVisionModeConsoleVars (name = VisionMode enum string). Toggling calls EnableMode + DevOnly_SelfSubscribe/Unsubscribe so the schedule runs even if no behavior subscribed. VisionSystem::Update requires color; UpdateGroundPlaneClassifier fills visualObstacles; VisionComponent::UpdateVisualObstacles calls MapComponent::AddDetectedObstacles. Distinct from prox-sensor “prox obstacles” and unexpected-movement obstacles. Needs calibrated camera and GroundPlaneClassifier config from vision_config.json. Costs CPU when forced on continuously.
Obstacles.howTo: 1) Set Obstacles true in console. 2) Ensure color frames are flowing (not power-save starving vision). 3) Watch nav map / logs for detected obstacle edges. 4) Turn off when done to free vision budget.

paths.notes: GroundPlaneClassifier block in vision_config.json configures the classifier used when Obstacles runs.

People.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::People. When on, the vision system runs the person_detector neural net (TFLite) on camera frames and reports Person salient points used by body-react / find-face-style behaviors.
People.detail: Same Vision.General.VisionModes console-var machinery as other VisionModes. People is registered to network name person_detector in visionModesHelpers. When the mode is enabled, VisionSystem collects networksToRun and StartProcessingIfIdle on the matching NeuralNetRunner; completed detections become SalientPointType::Person and mark People processed. Behaviors such as FindFaceAndThen and ConditionSalientPointDetected can also subscribe at Low/Med frequency without this toggle. Force-on is for testing person detection without waiting for those behaviors. Requires neural-net models from vision_config (graphFile under person_detector). Heavy on CPU/NPU vs pure classic CV modes.
People.howTo: 1) Set People true. 2) Confirm person_detector model is present in vision assets. 3) Point camera at a person; watch salient-point / behavior reactions or NeuralNetRunner_SaveImages for debug PNGs. 4) Disable when finished.

paths.notes: NeuralNets.Models entry networkName person_detector (TFLite graph + person-labels.txt).

SlowLoopBeginSize_loops.blurb: Dev override for how many slow counting-loop animation cycles play at the start of the counting animation (each loop covers two counts). Default −1 means “use the value from behavior JSON.” Set ≥ 0 to force that many begin-slow loops when the counting behavior activates.
SlowLoopBeginSize_loops.detail: BehaviorCountingAnimation (category BehaviorCountingAnimation). JSON keys SlowLoopBeginSize / SlowLoopEndSize set InstanceConfig defaults (code default 1 if missing). On activation SetCountParameters copies the console var into config only when ≥ 0, then partitions the remaining count target into slow-begin, fast-middle, and slow-end loops (loop count × 2 = counts covered). Only applies when something activates counting with SetCountTarget (e.g. count-related gameplay). Leave at −1 for production config-driven timing.
SlowLoopBeginSize_loops.statusNote: Only applied when BehaviorCountingAnimation activates and value ≥ 0; −1 leaves JSON config alone.

SlowLoopEndSize_loops.blurb: Dev override for how many slow counting-loop animation cycles play at the end of the counting animation (each loop covers two counts). Default −1 = use behavior JSON. Set ≥ 0 to force that many end-slow loops on the next counting activation.
SlowLoopEndSize_loops.detail: Sibling of SlowLoopBeginSize_loops. Same SetCountParameters path: if ≥ 0, overrides InstanceConfig.slowLoopEndSize_loops before remaining counts are split into begin slow / fast / end slow. After the end slow loops, CountingGetOut (optional TTS announcement) always plays. Only meaningful while counting behavior is used.
SlowLoopEndSize_loops.statusNote: Only applied when BehaviorCountingAnimation activates and value ≥ 0; −1 leaves JSON config alone.

Stats.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::Stats. When on, each vision pass computes a subsampled mean gray level (imageMean) for the frame and attaches it to processed-image results / RobotProcessedImage messages. Lightweight diagnostics, not a detector.
Stats.detail: Vision.General.VisionModes console toggle (SetupVisionModeConsoleVars). VisionSystem::ComputeMean samples gray ImageCache every ImageMeanSampleInc pixels and stores result.imageMean; modesProcessed includes Stats. VisionComponent later puts that mean into RobotProcessedImage only when Stats was processed. Default product schedules may already enable Stats periodically via visionScheduleMediator_config — this console force-on keeps it continuous for testing. Does not drive auto-exposure (AE uses its own histogram).

TimeToBeUpsideDown_ms.blurb: Self-test (factory/dev pickup check): how long (milliseconds) the robot must stay upside-down before cliff sensors are evaluated. Default 2000 ms. Prevents a brief flip from counting as the held-upside-down cliff test.
TimeToBeUpsideDown_ms.detail: SelfTestConfig static exposed under category SelfTest via WRAP_EXTERN_CONSOLE_VAR. BehaviorSelfTestPickup watches IMU Z accel ≤ kUpsideDownZAccel; once inverted long enough, it requires all four cliff sensors detecting cliff and raw values below threshold for SUCCESS. Separate from UpsideDownTimeout_ms (max time allowed after first inversion before fail). Only runs during self-test pickup sequence, not freeplay.

TimeUnobservedBeforeReLoggingToDAS_ms.blurb: If a stable face has not been seen for at least this long (default 10000 ms = 10 s), the next re-observation logs a DAS “persistent_session_only” re-see event. Named and stable session-only faces both qualify via HasStableID.
TimeUnobservedBeforeReLoggingToDAS_ms.detail: In FaceWorld observation handling, after immediate-recognition and first-stable-session DAS branches, if timeSinceLastSeen_ms exceeds this threshold and HasStableID(), a DAS message is sent with face ID and whether the face is named. Suppresses spam while continuously tracking the same person; re-arms after a gap. Pair with NumTimesToSeeFrontalToBeStable for when unnamed faces become eligible for this path.

UseButtonToStart.blurb: Factory playpen: when true (default), playpen wait-to-start will not finish until the backpack power button has been pressed (and charger/touch conditions also pass). When false, the button is not required to start playpen.
UseButtonToStart.detail: PlaypenConfig bool, WRAP_EXTERN_CONSOLE_VAR category Playpen. BehaviorPlaypenWaitToStart computes buttonGood = !kUseButtonToStart || (kUseButtonToStart && _buttonPressed). Combined with optional touch-to-start (kUseTouchToStart, default false) and a requirement that the robot is on charger contacts or charging. On success clears face text and sets FactoryTestResultCode::SUCCESS. Factory/dev only — not freeplay. Related: kUseTouchToStart, kTouchDurationToStart_ms.
